description:
Runs Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and other terminal coding agents together on one mission.

Runner is a native desktop application where terminal agents work together. Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Grok Build, Antigravity CLI, Copilot CLI and pi can take the same task in one mission, and each agent keeps its own TUI in a real terminal while the lead brings the decisions back to you. Everything in Runner is also a `runner` command: missions, crews, roles, projects, chats, sessions and messages are all addressable from the command line, with `runnerd` as the background service. Agents run natively on Windows without WSL, and PowerShell 7 is optional. Status: alpha, actively shipping. Native builds target macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows (x64) on Windows 10 version 1809 or later; Intel Macs, Windows ARM64 and Linux are not supported. The installer, the application and the CLI sidecars are Authenticode-signed with a Certum open-source certificate issued to Open Source Developer Yicheng Wang.
Runner 0.16.4 is a feature release for macOS and Windows on top of 0.16.3.
New
- Runner in English or Simplified Chinese. Choose a language in Settings → General → Language: System (the default, which follows your operating system's preferred language), English, or 简体中文. The change applies right away to every open window, including menus and the command palette, without a restart. Drafts, selections, shortcuts and terminal sessions are kept as they were. Agent output and terminal content are not translated. (#565)
- About Runner on macOS. The Runner menu now has About Runner above Check for Updates…. It opens the standard macOS About panel with Runner's version and build. (#924)
Bug fixes
- Codex mission members keep receiving messages. A Codex member could stop receiving messages after its first turn, including your answer to its question, if Codex switched to a different conversation during that turn or the turn failed without finishing. Runner now treats either case as the end of the turn and delivers the queued messages. (#927, #928)
- Paused missions no longer show an unread dot. The green unread dot is hidden while a mission is paused. It comes back when you resume the mission if responses are still unread. (#920, #923)
